about:
Infraredx, based in Bedford, Massachusetts, has been developing intravascular imaging technologies for nearly 30 years. The company was acquired by Nipro Corporation in 2015 and operates as a subsidiary within Nipro's Vascular Division. Founders are not publicly named; the current president and CEO is Stephen Sum, PhD, who joined the company as a senior algorithm scientist and advanced through R&D and regulatory roles.

The company designs and manufactures catheter-based imaging systems that combine intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). Its flagship Makoto platform integrates high-resolution structural imaging with plaque compositional analysis, while the Clarispro HD-IVUS and Dualpro IVUS+NIRS systems address specific clinical needs. Essential accessories support the imaging catheters. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

Infraredx serves interventional cardiologists, hospital catheterization labs, and vascular researchers focused on identifying high-risk lipid-core plaques. The technology is used in clinical studies such as SPECTAL and COLOR, which supported 510(k) clearances. Customers include opinion leaders in cardiology who collaborate on defining new standards of care.

The company positions itself as a pioneer in conquering vascular disease, emphasizing the combination of structural and compositional imaging to provide unprecedented treatment insights. Its differentiation rests on detecting unstable plaques that can lead to major adverse cardiac events and delivering best-in-class vessel visualization.
